threads.title: Liability frameworks for debris-generating manoeuvres
threads.body: Who bears responsibility when avoidance manoeuvres fail and generate debris? Current international space law is silent on this — the Outer Space Treaty assigns liability for damage but doesn't address the scenario where a state actor attempts compliance and inadvertently creates a new hazard. I've been drafting a framework that assigns proportional liability based on manoeuvre intent and outcome. Would value input from the Circle before I formalise this as a proposal.
threads.author: Akello Jane

threads.title: Psychological design in confined habitats
threads.body: Lessons from Antarctic stations for Mars habitat design. After reviewing 14 months of winterover data from Concordia and Halley VI, I'm seeing consistent patterns in crew psychological deterioration around months 4–6. Key factors: loss of circadian cues, reduced spatial variety, and social fatigue from fixed small-group interaction. These map directly to long-duration transit scenarios. Proposal: can we form a cross-domain working group to translate Antarctic habitability data into Mars transit design constraints?
threads.author: Namugga Claire

threads.title: Sentinel-2 data access for East Africa
threads.body: Current limitations and workarounds for remote sensing data access. The Copernicus Open Access Hub is reliable but throughput for East African users is poor — average download times for L2A tiles are 3–5x longer than for European endpoints. I've been testing a mirror setup via Kenya's KEPSA network that cuts this to parity. Sharing my config and benchmark results here. If anyone wants to test the mirror, ping me.
threads.author: Mwenda Thomas

threads.title: ITU coordination procedures — a plain language walkthrough
threads.body: Step-by-step guide to ITU frequency coordination for emerging space nations. I've written this as a practical walkthrough based on our experience coordinating the Ugandan ground station allocation. Covers: filing requirements, coordination simulation, objection windows, and the hidden pitfalls that trip up first-time filers. This is meant to be a living document — please suggest corrections or additions.
threads.author: Akello Jane

threads.title: Artemis Accords — East African perspective
threads.body: The Artemis Accords represent a framework for international cooperation in lunar exploration and beyond. Uganda, as an emerging spacefaring nation, stands to benefit from joining, but there are sovereignty concerns worth discussing. Article 10 on resource extraction could conflict with our existing mineral rights frameworks. However, the cooperation benefits for capacity building are significant. What's the collective view — should we push for an East African consensus position?
threads.author: Osei Kwame

threads.title: SAR interferometry for ground subsidence mapping
threads.body: I've been processing Sentinel-1 SAR data over the Kampala metropolitan area using InSAR time-series analysis. The results show subsidence rates of 5–12 mm/year in several built-up areas, consistent with groundwater extraction patterns. This has implications for infrastructure planning and could feed into our East Africa mapping project. Sharing preliminary interferograms — would appreciate remote sensing circle members reviewing the processing chain.
threads.author: Kimani Aisha

threads.title: Microgravity fluid dynamics — open dataset
threads.body: I've compiled a dataset of fluid behaviour experiments from ISS research (2018–2025) that's been processed into a format suitable for machine learning training. Covers capillary flow, Marangoni convection, and boiling dynamics. 14 GB total, CC-BY licensed. Looking for collaborators to help annotate the实验 conditions and build a prediction model. Any physics or CS members interested?
threads.author: Okello Robert

threads.title: End-of-life satellite deorbiting: who pays?
threads.body: As LEO becomes more congested, the question of who bears the cost of deorbiting defunct satellites is becoming urgent. Current IADC guidelines recommend deorbit within 25 years, but there's no enforcement mechanism and no funding model. I'm working on a proposal for a commons-managed deorbiting fund that would pool contributions from satellite operators proportional to their orbital footprint. Thoughts on the incentive structure?

cells.title: Debris liability framework — who bears responsibility?

messages.author: Akello J.
messages.text: The core issue is that current liability frameworks assume clear fault attribution. But manoeuvre-induced debris is different — the actor was attempting compliance. We need a proportional liability model based on intent and outcome.

messages.author: Osei Kwame
messages.text: What about the precedent from maritime law? The COLREGS framework assigns proportional liability in collision avoidance scenarios. Could we adapt that model for orbital manoeuvres?

messages.author: Mwenda Thomas
messages.text: From a remote sensing perspective — tracking manoeuvre intent requires telemetry data. Can we require operators to submit manoeuvre intent filings before execution? That creates an auditable record.

messages.author: Namugga Claire
messages.text: I'd support a graduated liability model: good-faith manoeuvres with debris generation → reduced liability; negligent manoeuvres → standard liability; intentional debris creation → enhanced liability. The intent filing would distinguish these.

draftResolutions.title: Debris liability framework — proportional model
draftResolutions.text:
MOTION: Establish proportional liability framework for manoeuvre-induced orbital debris

1. Operators must file manoeuvre intent with telemetry data before execution
2. Liability classification: good-faith (reduced), negligent (standard), intentional (enhanced)
3. Intent filing creates auditable record for post-incident assessment
4. Framework applies to all orbital operators within Commons jurisdiction
5. Enforcement through existing policy resolution mechanisms

cells.title: System Settings: Steward Term Extension to 18 months

settingsChanges.rationale: 12 months is too short for stewards to build expertise and deliver meaningful results. Extension to 18 months allows for a full project cycle.
With longer terms, allowing a third consecutive term maintains continuity for complex governance areas.

messages.author: Ssempa D.
